Archive item 1: Microfilm Records of the National Library Board: Baptismal Certificates
Source format: Microfilm records

Requested by: Mrs. Peggy Wong (Reader’s Ticket No. 1187)
Date of Request: 2025-03-04T09:00:00+08:00
Purpose of Request: Genealogical research on the Tan family of Upper Serangoon; verification of baptismal entries for the period 1888–1892.
Reel Returned: 2025-03-04T13:40:00+08:00

NOTES ON REEL CONTENTS

The reel contains 214 frames covering baptisms, marriages, and burials recorded at the Church of the Holy Family between January 1888 and December 1892. The register pages are numbered consecutively, with occasional gaps where pages were torn or stained. Entries are handwritten in a mixture of English and Portuguese creole, with some Latin marginalia. The priest’s hand is consistent for most of the period, with a noticeable change in script style beginning in mid-1890, likely indicating a new parish priest.

Baptismal entries typically include the date of baptism, the child’s name, the parents’ names, the godparents’ names, and the date of birth where known. In some cases, the birth date is omitted, and the entry records only the baptismal date. The register also includes annotations in a later hand, likely from the 1920s, adding or correcting information in pencil.

FRAME-BY-FRAME SUMMARY (SELECTED ENTRIES)

Frame 0012 – 1888-03-16
Baptism of Maria da Silva, daughter of Joaquim da Silva and Anna de Souza. Godparents: Francisco Rodrigues and Isabel da Costa. Born 1888-03-02. Marginal note in pencil: “Married 1912, St. Joseph’s Church.”

Frame 0015 – 1888-03-18
Baptism of Tan Ah Kow, son of Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo (also recorded as “Lim Neo, daughter of Lim Ah Chye”). Godparents: Chua Kim Seng and Tan Swee Neo. The baptismal record for Tan Ah Kow, found on microfilm at the National Library Board, lists his birth_date as 1888-03-14. Record status: current. This entry is the current authoritative record for the birth date of Tan Ah Kow and is cited in subsequent family histories. The priest’s notation in the margin reads: “Natus est 14 Martii 1888.” The entry is in good condition, with no erasures or corrections.

Frame 0016 – 1888-03-18
Baptism of Tan Ah Hock, son of Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Godparents: Chua Kim Seng and Tan Swee Neo. Born 1888-03-14. This entry is immediately adjacent to that of Tan Ah Kow, suggesting the baptism of twins or siblings on the same day. No annotation distinguishes the two children beyond their names.

Frame 0019 – 1888-04-01
Baptism of Maria Tan, daughter of Tan Ah Kow and Chua Kim Neo. Godparents: Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Born 1888-03-20. The presence of this entry is anomalous; the godparents are the same as those listed for Tan Ah Kow’s baptism in Frame 0015, and the child’s father bears the same name as the infant in that entry. This may indicate a recording error, or the existence of two individuals named Tan Ah Kow in the same parish. The matter is left unresolved in the register.

Frame 0022 – 1888-04-08
Baptism of Lim Chye Neo, daughter of Lim Ah Chye and Chua Soon Neo. Godparents: Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Born 1888-03-28.

Frame 0027 – 1888-05-06
Baptism of Joseph Pereira, son of Manuel Pereira and Maria de Rosario. Godparents: Antonio d’Souza and Rosa Pereira. Born 1888-05-01.

Frame 0031 – 1888-06-17
Baptism of Tan Boon Seng, son of Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Godparents: Chua Kim Seng and Tan Swee Neo. Born 1888-06-10. This entry records a third child of Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo within the same year, following Tan Ah Kow and Tan Ah Hock in March.

Frame 0035 – 1888-07-01
Baptism of Anna de Cruz, daughter of Pedro de Cruz and Maria de Conceicao. Godparents: Joaquim da Silva and Anna de Souza. Born 1888-06-24. No birth date is recorded; the entry lists only the baptismal date.
Frame 0038 – 1888-07-15
Baptism of Maria Tan, daughter of Tan Ah Kow and Chua Kim Neo. Godparents: Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Born 1888-07-08. The register contains a second entry for a Maria Tan with the same parentage, the first being recorded in Frame 0019. The priest has written in the margin: “Duplicata,” indicating a deliberate copy rather than a separate child. The earlier entry is marked with a small cross and the word “erasa” in pencil, though no erasure is visible on the film. The duplicate is the current authoritative record for this baptism.

Frame 0042 – 1888-08-05
Baptism of Lim Ah Kow, son of Lim Ah Chye and Chua Soon Neo. Godparents: Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Born 1888-07-28. This is the second child of Lim Ah Chye and Chua Soon Neo recorded in this register, following Lim Chye Neo in Frame 0022. The godparents are again Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo, a pattern observed across multiple families in this period.

Frame 0045 – 1888-09-02
Baptism of Chong Kim Neo, daughter of Chong Ah Kow and Tan Swee Neo. Godparents: Chua Kim Seng and Tan Cheng Huat. Born 1888-08-25. No annotation. The entry is clear and complete.

Frame 0049 – 1888-10-07
Baptism of Joseph de Souza, son of Antonio d’Souza and Rosa Pereira. Godparents: Manuel Pereira and Maria de Rosario. Born 1888-09-30. The godparents are the same couple who appear in Frame 0027 as parents of Joseph Pereira, indicating close family ties between the Pereira and d’Souza households.

Frame 0053 – 1888-11-04
Baptism of Tan Chye Neo, daughter of Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Godparents: Chua Kim Seng and Tan Swee Neo. Born 1888-10-28. This is the fourth child of Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo recorded in this register within the year. The repetition of the same godparents for each child suggests they are relatives of the family.

Frame 0057 – 1888-12-02
Baptism of Anna Pereira, daughter of Manuel Pereira and Maria de Rosario. Godparents: Antonio d’Souza and Rosa Pereira. Born 1888-11-25. The entry is in good condition. The priest’s handwriting is consistent with earlier frames.

Frame 0061 – 1889-01-06
Baptism of Tan Ah Hock, son of Tan Ah Kow and Chua Kim Neo. Godparents: Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Born 1888-12-30. This entry is the second child of Tan Ah Kow and Chua Kim Neo recorded in this register, following the duplicate Maria Tan entry in Frame 0038. The godparents are the same as those for the earlier entries of this family.

Frame 0065 – 1889-02-03
Baptism of Lim Boon Seng, son of Lim Ah Chye and Chua Soon Neo. Godparents: Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Born 1889-01-27. The third child of Lim Ah Chye and Chua Soon Neo. The pattern of godparents remains the same.

Frame 0068 – 1889-03-10
Baptism of Maria de Rosario, daughter of Pedro de Cruz and Maria de Conceicao. Godparents: Joaquim da Silva and Anna de Souza. Born 1889-03-03. This is the second child of Pedro de Cruz and Maria de Conceicao recorded in this register, following Anna de Cruz in Frame 0035.

Frame 0072 – 1889-04-14
Baptism of Tan Swee Neo, daughter of Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Godparents: Chua Kim Seng and Tan Swee Neo. Born 1889-04-07. The fifth child of Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. The godmother, Tan Swee Neo, shares the same name as the child, suggesting the godmother is a close relative.

Frame 0076 – 1889-05-12
Baptism of Joseph Tan, son of Tan Ah Kow and Chua Kim Neo. Godparents: Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Born 1889-05-05. The third child of Tan Ah Kow and Chua Kim Neo. The entry is clear and complete.

Frame 0080 – 1889-06-09
Baptism of Anna d’Souza, daughter of Antonio d’Souza and Rosa Pereira. Godparents: Manuel Pereira and Maria de Rosario. Born 1889-06-02. The second child of Antonio d’Souza and Rosa Pereira recorded in this register.

----- end of archived item -----

documents.content:
Requested by: Mrs. Peggy Wong (Reader’s Ticket No. 1187)
Date of Request: 2025-03-04T09:00:00+08:00
Purpose of Request: Genealogical research on the Tan family of Upper Serangoon; verification of baptismal entries for the period 1888–1892.
Reel Returned: 2025-03-04T13:40:00+08:00

NOTES ON REEL CONTENTS

The reel contains 214 frames covering baptisms, marriages, and burials recorded at the Church of the Holy Family between January 1888 and December 1892. The register pages are numbered consecutively, with occasional gaps where pages were torn or stained. Entries are handwritten in a mixture of English and Portuguese creole, with some Latin marginalia. The priest’s hand is consistent for most of the period, with a noticeable change in script style beginning in mid-1890, likely indicating a new parish priest.

Baptismal entries typically include the date of baptism, the child’s name, the parents’ names, the godparents’ names, and the date of birth where known. In some cases, the birth date is omitted, and the entry records only the baptismal date. The register also includes annotations in a later hand, likely from the 1920s, adding or correcting information in pencil.

FRAME-BY-FRAME SUMMARY (SELECTED ENTRIES)

Frame 0012 – 1888-03-16
Baptism of Maria da Silva, daughter of Joaquim da Silva and Anna de Souza. Godparents: Francisco Rodrigues and Isabel da Costa. Born 1888-03-02. Marginal note in pencil: “Married 1912, St. Joseph’s Church.”

Frame 0015 – 1888-03-18
Baptism of Tan Ah Kow, son of Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo (also recorded as “Lim Neo, daughter of Lim Ah Chye”). Godparents: Chua Kim Seng and Tan Swee Neo. The baptismal record for Tan Ah Kow, found on microfilm at the National Library Board, lists his birth_date as 1888-03-14. Record status: current. This entry is the current authoritative record for the birth date of Tan Ah Kow and is cited in subsequent family histories. The priest’s notation in the margin reads: “Natus est 14 Martii 1888.” The entry is in good condition, with no erasures or corrections.

Frame 0016 – 1888-03-18
Baptism of Tan Ah Hock, son of Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Godparents: Chua Kim Seng and Tan Swee Neo. Born 1888-03-14. This entry is immediately adjacent to that of Tan Ah Kow, suggesting the baptism of twins or siblings on the same day. No annotation distinguishes the two children beyond their names.

Frame 0019 – 1888-04-01
Baptism of Maria Tan, daughter of Tan Ah Kow and Chua Kim Neo. Godparents: Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Born 1888-03-20. The presence of this entry is anomalous; the godparents are the same as those listed for Tan Ah Kow’s baptism in Frame 0015, and the child’s father bears the same name as the infant in that entry. This may indicate a recording error, or the existence of two individuals named Tan Ah Kow in the same parish. The matter is left unresolved in the register.

Frame 0022 – 1888-04-08
Baptism of Lim Chye Neo, daughter of Lim Ah Chye and Chua Soon Neo. Godparents: Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Born 1888-03-28.

Frame 0027 – 1888-05-06
Baptism of Joseph Pereira, son of Manuel Pereira and Maria de Rosario. Godparents: Antonio d’Souza and Rosa Pereira. Born 1888-05-01.

Frame 0031 – 1888-06-17
Baptism of Tan Boon Seng, son of Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo. Godparents: Chua Kim Seng and Tan Swee Neo. Born 1888-06-10. This entry records a third child of Tan Cheng Huat and Lim Neo within the same year, following Tan Ah Kow and Tan Ah Hock in March.

**Agenda**

2. Matters arising

4. Proposed exhibition: "Tampines: From Kampung to Town" (July 2025)
5. Volunteer recruitment and training schedule
6. Budget review for Q1 2025
7. Any other matters
8. Date of next meeting

---

**1. Confirmation of Previous Minutes**
The minutes of the meeting held on 16 January 2025 (HC/2025/01/03) were circulated to all members by email on 28 January 2025. No amendments were proposed. The minutes were confirmed as a true and accurate record.
*Action: Secretary to file signed copy in the Committee binder.*

**2. Matters Arising**
2.1 **Oral History Project – Interview Consent Forms**
Mr. Wong Chee Meng reported that 12 of the 15 consent forms for the oral history interviews have been returned. The remaining three are from interviewees who have requested a Malay-language version of the form. Mr. Wong will follow up with the translated copies by 25 February 2025.

2.2 **Heritage Resource Centre – Air-Conditioning Fault**
Ms. Lim Geok Hoon noted that the air-conditioning in the Resource Centre has been intermittent since early February. The estate management office has been notified, and a technician is scheduled to inspect the unit on 24 February 2025 at 10:00 a.m. The Committee agreed to keep the Resource Centre closed to the public during the inspection.

2.3 **Heritage Trail Brochure (Historical)**
The previous version of the Heritage Trail brochure (printed December 2024) contained an outdated bus route map. The revised brochure, updated with the new bus service 129 route, has been approved for reprinting. The Committee noted that the old brochure stock will be pulped and not distributed.

**3. Progress Update on Oral History Project (Phase 2)**
Tan Siew Lan, Volunteer Coordinator, presented the status of Phase 2 of the Oral History Project.

3.1 **Interviews Completed**
As of 18 February 2025, 18 interviews have been completed out of the target of 25 for Phase 2. The completed interviews cover residents who lived in the Tampines area between 1965 and 1985.

3.2 **Recording Quality**
Two recordings (OHP-2025-014 and OHP-2025-017) were found to have background noise that affected audio clarity. The recordings have been flagged for re-recording if the interviewees are willing. Ms. Tan will contact the interviewees by 28 February 2025 to arrange possible re-recording sessions.

3.3 **Transcription Timeline**
Transcripts for the first 10 interviews are expected to be completed by 15 March 2025. The Committee noted that the transcription contractor, Mr. Lim Soon Huat, has confirmed his availability.

**4. Heritage Exhibition "Tampines: From Kampung to Town"**

4.1 **Exhibition Dates**

Mr. Tan Boon Heng, Research Lead, presented the finalised schedule for the Heritage Exhibition. The exhibition will be held at the Tampines Regional Library, Level 1 Exhibition Hall. The committee meeting minutes state that the Heritage Committee's exhibition_date_start is 2025-04-01. Record status: current. This date is current and confirmed by the library management.

The exhibition will run from 1 April 2025 to 30 April 2025, with the following key dates:

- 1 April 2025 – Exhibition opens to the public
- 5 April 2025 – Official opening ceremony and reception
- 12 April 2025 – Guided tour for invited school groups
- 19 April 2025 – Public guided tour (registration required)
- 26 April 2025 – Closing event and volunteer appreciation

4.2 **Exhibition Panels**

Mr. Tan Boon Heng presented the draft layout of the exhibition panels. The exhibition will consist of 12 panels covering the following themes:

1. Introduction – Tampines in the 1960s
2. The Kampung Landscape
3. Farming and Livelihoods
4. The Tampines River and Flooding
5. The Sand Quarry and Its Workers
6. Community Life – Markets, Festivals, and Neighbours
7. Schools and Education
8. The Tampines Road
9. Resettlement and the Move to HDB Flats
10. The New Town Takes Shape
11. Tampines Today
12. Looking Forward – Memories and the Future

The Committee reviewed the draft text for each panel. Several suggestions were made:

- Ms. Lim Geok Hoon suggested that Panel 4 include a map showing the location of the Tampines River and the areas affected by flooding. Mr. Tan Boon Heng agreed to incorporate this.
- Mr. Wong Chee Meng noted that Panel 9 should mention the role of the Tampines Town Council in the early resettlement process. Mr. Tan Boon Heng will check the draft text and amend as necessary.
- Ms. Nurul Fatin suggested adding a small section on Panel 6 about the contributions of Malay and Indian residents to community life. The Committee agreed this would strengthen the panel.

4.3 **Exhibition Artefacts**

Mr. Tan Boon Heng reported on the artefacts that have been secured for display:

- A collection of photographs from the National Archives of Singapore (NAS-1948-0345, NAS-1952-0117, NAS-1960-0233)
- A traditional wooden fishing net donated by Mr. Lim Ah Kow
- A set of weighing scales from the former Tampines market
- A school uniform and textbooks from the former Tampines Primary School
- A collection of household items from a kampung house, including a clay stove and cooking pots

The Chairperson welcomed all members and guests. He noted that this would be the final meeting before the exhibition opening on 5 April 2025 and thanked everyone for their efforts over the past months.

## 2. Confirmation of Previous Minutes

The minutes of the meeting held on 10 March 2025 were circulated with the agenda. There were no amendments proposed.

**Resolution:** The minutes were confirmed as a true record.

---

## 3. Matters Arising

### 3.1 Artefact Loans – Follow-up

Mr. Tan Boon Heng reported that all artefact loan agreements had been signed and returned. The National Archives of Singapore (NAS) photographs (NAS-1948-0345, NAS-1952-0117, NAS-1960-0233) had been received in good condition and were being stored in the climate-controlled display cases at the venue.

The wooden fishing net donated by Mr. Lim Ah Kow had been treated for woodworm and was ready for display. Mr. Tan noted that Mr. Lim was unable to attend today's meeting but had sent his best wishes for the exhibition.

### 3.2 Exhibition Panels – Revisions

Mr. Tan Boon Heng confirmed that all revisions suggested at the previous meeting had been incorporated into the panel drafts:

- Panel 4 now includes a map of the Tampines River and the areas affected by flooding.
- Panel 9 has been amended to include the role of the Tampines Town Council in the early resettlement process.
- Panel 6 now includes a section on the contributions of Malay and Indian residents to community life.

Ms. Lim Geok Hoon requested that the map on Panel 4 be checked for accuracy, as she had noticed a minor discrepancy in the positioning of the former sand quarry relative to the river. Mr. Tan agreed to verify this with the National Archives cartographic team before final printing.

### 3.3 Volunteer Training

Ms. Nurul Fatin reported that 14 volunteers had been trained for the guided tours scheduled for 12 and 19 April 2025. A further two training sessions would be held on 29 March and 2 April 2025 at the venue. Volunteers would be briefed on the exhibition content, handling of visitor queries, and emergency procedures.

---

| 10:45 a.m. | Guided tour of the exhibition for VIPs |
| 11:30 a.m. | Light refreshments and networking |
| 12:00 p.m. | End of official programme |

Ms. Lim confirmed that the invitation cards had been printed and would be dispatched by 28 March 2025. A total of 220 invitations had been sent, with 145 acceptances received to date. Members were asked to remind their contacts to RSVP by 31 March 2025.

The Committee discussed the catering arrangements. Ms. Peggy Lee suggested that a halal-certified caterer be engaged, given the diverse backgrounds of the invited guests. The Committee agreed. Ms. Lim said she would approach two caterers for quotations and confirm by 28 March 2025.
